title: Orient Express Launches Its First Cruise Ship: The Luxurious 54-Cabin Corinthian - AOL
extractedText: Orient Express Launches Its First Cruise Ship: The Luxurious 54-Cabin CorinthianMeghann FoyeFri, June 12, 2026 at 1:10 PM UTC0If your ultimate travel bucket list has always included a journey on the world's most glamorous historic train, you're going to want to pack your bags for a completely different kind of voyage. The legendary name that once defined the golden age of luxury rail travel is officially taking to the high seas, and it's bringing a staggering dose of old-world European romance along with it.Orient Express and world-renowned shipbuilders Chantiers de l'Atlantique have officially christened the Orient Express Corinthian, a magnificent 720-foot, 26,600-gross-ton vessel that holds the title of the world's largest sailing yacht.Fresh off its spring baptism in France, the stunning ship has already made its first glamorous splash, turning heads offshore just days ago as it cruised past the crowds at the Monaco Grand Prix. The hybrid-powered vessel will spend its inaugural season exploring the chicest harbors of the Mediterranean before crossing the Atlantic for a winter of island-hopping through the Caribbean.While the ship looks like a nostalgic dream straight out of the 1920s, the technology powering it is purely futuristic. The vessel is the world's first cruise ship equipped with a revolutionary rigid wind propulsion system featuring three automated sails that tower over 320 feet in the air. Because these massive structures rotate a full 360 degrees to capture the wind, the ship can achieve 100% wind-powered propulsion under favorable conditions—clocking a cool 12 knots under sail alone during its recent sea trials."This new ship is a concrete, technical response to the decarbonisation challenges facing maritime transport," said Laurent Castaing, Chief Executive Officer of Chantiers de l'Atlantique, noting that the eco-conscious design is the result of 10 years of intense research and development.Related: The Luxe Venice Simplon-Orient-Express Is Adding an Enchanting New RouteAdvertisementA Floating, Hyper-Exclusive Boutique HotelSEBASTIEN SALOM-GOMIS / Contributor via GettyThe ship sheds any typical mega-resort cruise ship aesthetic to feel like a private, ultra-luxury estate. Creative Director Maxime d'Angeac led a massive team of close to 2,000 French artisans to design an interior of quiet refinement, resulting in just 54 jaw-dropping suites swathed in rich leather, precious wood veneers and stunning marble. To maximize that sense of airy grandeur, each cabin comes with a dedicated butler, a massive 3.60-meter panoramic window and ceilings that sit significantly higher than current cruise industry standards.The onboard amenities read like a luxury traveler's ultimate wish list. The fully inclusive experience boasts five restaurants and private dining rooms helmed by multi-Michelin-starred chef Yannick Alléno, eight distinct bars—including a hidden Art Deco speakeasy—a 115-seat cabaret theater, a private recording studio, and a serene Guerlain spa. Outside, passengers can lounge by a sleek 16.5-meter swimming lane or utilize the ship's private marina for direct, effortless ocean access.Related: These Are the 10 New Cruise Ships Everyone Will Be Talking About"Bringing Orient Express to the sea fits naturally within the imagination of this legendary brand: a journey rooted in discovery, unhurried time, excellence, and elegance," said Sébastien Bazin, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Accor. "This sailing vessel proudly showcases the very best of French expertise and craftsmanship."If you want to experience the slow-travel voyage for yourself, the Orient Express Corinthian will spend the summer and early autumn exploring the harbors and quieter shores of the Mediterranean and Adriatic seas. By late autumn, the ship will cross the Atlantic to spend the winter island-hopping through the sunny Caribbean, offering highly flexible itineraries of one to four nights that can be combined into an entirely customized getaway.Related: A Major Cruise Line Is Quietly Turning Its Youngest Passengers Into 'Ocean Ambassadors'This story was originally published by Parade on Jun 12, 2026, where it first appeared in the Travel section.
